title: Nanoscale Insights into Charge Trap Layer Engineering in Flash Memory Devices
content: As technological demands evolve, understanding the material design of flash memory devices is critical to enhancing their performance, scalability, and reliability. Key structural components, including the charge trap layer (CTL), tunnel oxide, blocking oxide, channel, and control gate, directly influence device efficiency, endurance, and data retention. Amorphous silicon nitride/silicon oxynitride systems, commonly employed in flash memory applications, have garnered significant research interest. Extensive theoretical studies have explored charge trapping mechanisms, attributing them to factors such as silicon dangling bonds and embedded silicon clusters [1-4]. These models suggest the presence of multiple defect states within the bandgap, driven by the amorphous nature of the material [5]. Despite the development of numerous theoretical frameworks, direct experimental validation of charge trapping mechanisms remains a challenge, limiting the precise engineering of these materials for next-generation memory devices.
